lint.assignInCond: Assignment instead of comparison: conditions compare with =.
lint.assignEq: Comparison instead of assignment: assign with := or <-.
lint.badLoopHead: Loop head cannot be read: “{0}” (e.g. “for i := 1 to 10” or “foreach x in array”).
lint.caseBool: Case selection on the condition “{0}” with the labels true/false. Better: a branch with the condition “{0}”. Reason: the two-way selection is meant for yes/no decisions and reads at a glance; the case selection is for several values of one expression.
lint.caseCond: Conditions as case labels (case true). Better: nested branches with the conditions {0}. Reason: a case selection checks an expression for fixed values; conditions usually belong in branches, and many languages only allow constants in case/switch.
lint.caseElseCond: The “else” branch is labeled with a condition (“{0}”). Reason: the branch runs without any check for all remaining cases – the label pretends a check.
lint.multiLine: Several statements in one block. Better: split the {0} statements into {0} blocks. Reason: one block per statement is common and clear; each step stays visible and can be stopped at on its own.
lint.emptyLoop: Empty loop body. Reason: a loop without statements does nothing or runs forever; empty blocks are only customary in branches.
lint.endless: Endless loop without leave, exit or return. Reason: the program never ends at this point.
lint.condUnchanged: The loop does not change {0}. Reason: the condition then always stays the same – the loop runs not at all or forever.
lint.unused: “{0}” gets a value that is never used. Reason: a superfluous statement or a typo in the name.
lint.unreachable: Never reached – preceded by “{0}”. Reason: statements after exit, return or leave are not executed.
lint.typeMix: “{0}” is sometimes text, sometimes a number. Reason: a variable should have exactly one type; Java, C and other typed languages do not allow the change.
lint.emptyBlock: Empty block. Reason: an empty block only makes sense in branches.
lint.noName: The structogram has no name. Reason: every structogram should be named so that it can be identified and called.
lint.untyped: “{0}” is created without a type. Better declare it first: “var {0}: {1}”. Reason: the type defines which values and operations are allowed – without it the first value or the input decides, errors show up late, and the generated code has to guess the type.
lint.declScopeBefore: “{0}” is not declared here – “{1}” is only inside {2}. Better: declare “{1}” before {2}. Reason: a declaration is valid from its position in its block on; “{0}” is also needed outside of it.
lint.declScopeBranch: “{0}” is not declared here – “{1}” is only in another branch of {2}. Better: also declare “{1}” at the start of this branch (or once before {2}). Reason: a declaration is valid from its position in its block on; this way the type of “{0}” is clear on every path.
lint.untypedDecl: “{0}” is declared without a type. Better: “{1}”. Reason: without a type the type only follows from the first value – readers have to work it out, and a later assignment of a different type goes unnoticed.
lint.untypedNoGuess: “{0}” is created without a type. Better declare it first: “var {0}: …” with the matching type, e.g. int, double or string. Reason: the type defines which values and operations are allowed – without it the first value or the input decides, errors show up late, and the generated code has to guess the type.
lint.untypedParam: Parameter “{0}” has no type. Better: “{1}”. Reason: callers cannot see which values are expected, and the generated code has to guess the type.
lint.untypedReturn: “{0}” returns a value but has no return type. Better: “{1}”. Reason: the return type is part of the subroutine's interface; without it callers and the generated code have to guess it.
lint.untypedVoid: “{0}” returns no value, but its signature does not say so. Better: “{1}”. Reason: with void it is clear at a glance that the subroutine returns nothing on purpose – and that the return type was not just forgotten.
lint.noPrompt: Input without a prompt. Better: INPUT "{0}: ", {0}. Reason: users only see a blinking cursor and do not know what to enter.
lint.floatEq: Decimal numbers compared with = or <> (“{0}”). Better: “{1}”. Reason: decimal numbers are stored rounded – 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 is false, for example; the suggestion checks whether both values are almost equal.
web.lint.none: No errors or hints in the structogram.
